nodes.description: Dnah17-/- males have MMAF with disorganized axonemes. They also have a sharp fall in sperm count, deformed elongating spermatid nuclei and spermiation failure with apoptosis, which are not reported in patients.
Mice homozygous for the mouse equivalent of p.C1803Y have normal sperm count and morphology but reduced motility and fewer pups, with doublet 4-7 loss in epididymal sperm.

The homozygous p.C1803Y (c.G5408A) missense allele reported in one consanguineous Pakistani family. Unlike null alleles, it does not remove DNAH17: the protein is still made and localizes normally to the sperm flagellum, and ODAs remain visible on the surviving doublets in knock-in mice. Motor function is presumed reduced rather than lost, and flagella form normally but are destabilized later.

nodes.description: ICSI bypasses the motility defect, but outcomes are poorer than for many other MMAF genes. Total fertilization failure has been reported, and in a review of 11 couples only three achieved clinical pregnancy, all with ICSI combined with assisted oocyte activation (AOA). A 2025 series reported transferable embryos without AOA in four couples, and a later series reported pregnancies with ICSI plus AOA. The fertilization defect may reflect impaired acrosome reaction and reduced sperm PLCZ1, but this is not established.

nodes.description: Nonsense, frameshift, splice and many missense alleles abolish or sharply reduce DNAH17 protein in sperm. Splice-site alleles can delete exons encoding the AAA6 part of the motor domain. The p.C1803Y missense allele is an exception, in which DNAH17 is still made and localizes normally to the flagellum; it is a separate hypomorphic node.
